name: CA-09
label: Safe D

The district leans Democratic by eight points on partisanship, and the 2024 environment adds further Democratic margin

model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: a Democratic-leaning Central Valley seat, a well-funded two-term incumbent, a lightly financed challenger, and markets pricing this near-certain for Harder. With no polls to contradict the fundamentals, the forecast stays close to the structural estimate of a roughly twenty-point Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any late surge of outside spending against Harder or unexpected polling showing a single-digit race would be the first sign this is closer than the fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Josh Harder, the Democratic incumbent in California's ninth district, seeks another term against Republican John McBride. The district has an eight-point Democratic partisan lean, and the national environment in 2024 adds to that advantage. Harder has raised more than $4 million and holds $4.7 million in cash, while McBride has raised about $52,000 with minimal outside support on either side.

No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters cover the race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals and money. Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price Harder as an overwhelming favorite, at 96 to 98 percent. The expected margin is roughly twenty points Democratic, with meaningful uncertainty given the absence of polling.
